A first stop before [Classic Sequencers Compared](sequencer-compare.qmd). Short sections, one idea each. Click a heading to fold or open it.

::: {.ik-do}
**What you'll do**

1. Read what the TB-303 pattern mode is and when it was made.
2. Learn its sound, one idea at a time.
3. Take a guided tour: press each **▶ Hear step** button and listen for one change.
4. Find records it is on.
5. Check yourself with a short quiz.
:::

## What it is

- The **TB-303** (Roland, 1981; Wikipedia, "Roland TB-303") has its own sequencer. A pattern is written in two passes.
- First, **pitch mode**: press the notes in order. Then **time mode**: say for each step if it is a note, a tie or a rest (TB-303 manual, pp. 4-5, 15).
- A pattern stores **pitch, length of note, accent and slide** (manual, pp. 4-5).
- For its sound, see [Meet the TB-303](intro-tb-303.qmd).

## Its sound

- The basic unit is the **sixteenth note**; a pattern has up to 16 steps (manual, p. 5).
- **Accent** makes a step louder and brighter; **slide** glides into the next note (manual, pp. 41-43).
- It stores **64 patterns** and 7 tracks (manual, pp. 11, 23).
- Here the voice is the page's own shared voice, not a model of the 303.

## Check yourself

Click an answer. You will see at once if it is right. Nothing is saved or sent.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>In which order do you write a 303 pattern?</b></p><ul><li>Pitch mode, then time mode</li><li>Time mode, then pitch mode</li><li>Both at once</li><li>With a microphone</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Manual pp. 4-5.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Time mode says whether a step is…</b></p><ul><li>A note, tie or rest</li><li>Loud or soft</li><li>Major or minor</li><li>Fast or slow</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Manual p. 15.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>A slide…</b></p><ul><li>Glides into the next note</li><li>Stops the pattern</li><li>Changes the drum</li><li>Adds reverb</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Step 4.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>The basic step is a…</b></p><ul><li>Sixteenth note</li><li>Whole note</li><li>Half note</li><li>Bar</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Manual p. 5.</p></div>
```

"Roland TB-303." *Wikipedia*, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roland_TB-303](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roland_TB-303). Sawtooth or square; a 24 dB-per-octave resonant low-pass filter that does not self-oscillate; 1981-1984.
